A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COMBRL research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C support a reliable comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original continuous-control experiments, downstream-task evaluations, reward-weight ablations, TaCoS experiments and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds Humanoid evaluations, a true-dynamics MPC reference and exploration diagnostics.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the reward-plus-uncertainty objective, the auto-tuning loss and the TaCoS adaptation remain unchanged. Expanded solver explanations and benchmark-specific network configurations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Figure 2 adds DMC-Humanoid Stand and Run to the existing Gym/DMC evaluations. The GP environments, downstream tasks and TaCoS environments are retained, making this a localized expansion of continuous-control coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 1 adds MPC using iCEM with known true dynamics as a reference for optimal-policy performance. The existing Mean Planning, PETS and OCORL comparisons remain; the Humanoid evaluations use the existing Mean Planning/PETS comparator set.

E3.justification: Figure 2 extends the reported Quadruped training horizon from one million to two million environment steps. New protocols evaluate Pendulum uncertainty on 100 random state-action pairs after each episode and CartPole uncertainty along executed trajectories. Table 4 specifies larger policy/critic networks for the added Humanoid evaluations.

E4.justification: New Figures 6 and 7 examine auto-tuned reward-weight evolution across six tasks and epistemic uncertainty in unsupervised Pendulum and reward-driven CartPole. These add targeted mechanism diagnostics; the existing reward-weight ablation, downstream analyses and adaptive-control comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: The stated five-seed GP and ten-seed ensemble/TaCoS evaluations retain mean and standard-error reporting. The added model-uncertainty diagnostics measure algorithm behavior rather than introduce a new procedure for estimating experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds Humanoid returns, true-dynamics MPC reference results, generally decreasing auto-tuned weights and uncertainty-reduction findings. Quadruped results extend to a larger training budget, so the later endpoint is not a same-budget gain. Figures 3–5, the TaCoS learning curves and Table 3 retain their results.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds the missing horizon factor T to Lemma 4's lambda, restores a missing 1/N factor and square root in Theorem 2's proof, and explains the claimed connection between lambda squared and model complexity. Lemma 4's derivation is shortened. The assumptions and stated asymptotic guarantees remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about uncertainty-guided exploration, regret and sample-complexity guarantees, scalability and downstream generalization. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly interprets observed auto-tuning decay as emphasizing exploration early and reducing it as learning stabilizes. Appendix C.6 interprets the uncertainty diagnostics as evidence of broader uncertainty reduction and exploration of informative states, elaborating the existing mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Table 4 adds Humanoid settings, including two 512-unit policy/critic layers and five dynamics networks with two 512-unit layers. Appendix C.6 documents the uncertainty-measurement procedure. Existing code access, hardware disclosures and retained experimental hyperparameters remain available.

R1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly cites Rubinstein (1999) when distinguishing iCEM from vanilla CEM. The active-learning references emphasized in the revised introduction already appeared in v1's Appendix A; the principal positioning against prior continuous-time and discrete-time methods is retained.

P1.justification: v2 expands the introductory motivation and SAC/iCEM explanations, edits experimental prose and cross-references, adds an uncertainty-analysis subsection and an LLM usage statement, and updates the publication header. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains an MPC reference and revised legend; Figure 2 expands from eight to ten panels. Two diagnostic figures are added and Table 4 is expanded. Existing figures are relocated, including the unchanged TaCoS learning curves renumbered from Figure 6 to Figure 8, while the document retains its basic layout.

improvement.justification: The added MPC reference, Humanoid evaluations and exploration diagnostics make the existing empirical claims easier to assess. Appendix B.2 also repairs specific algebraic errors, although shortening Lemma 4 removes an explicit derivation. These provide a limited net improvement in supporting evidence and clarity without substantially changing the research.
